messages:
monitoring-bot: ALERT: rapid GPU ECC/Xid error spike detected across us-west2 and us-central. Auto-drain policy triggered on ~120 GPUs (affected capacity ~21%). See /alerts/1798765432 for details.
ajay-sre: seeing the same in Prometheus panels, queueing depth jumped ~18%. Can someone pause auto-drain?
maria-ops: I’m on it. pausing policy via infra-control: `infractl policy set auto-drain false --scope region:us-west2,us-central`
ops-oncall: thanks — pausing now. Confirmed auto-drain halted.
lucas-runtime: logs show a lot of `Xid: 13` plus `ECC corrected` churn, but the rate is odd: many hosts reporting identical sample windows. suspect telemetry duplication.
emily-devex: source of truth check: kernel logs on a sample host show only a handful of actual XID errors during the window. Telemetry counts seem inflated.
ajay-sre: upload a host trace pls. if counts are inflated we might have a metrics pipeline bug; otherwise this is actual hardware flakiness and we need to keep drains.
maria-ops: pasted condensed logs for host gpu-node-12: ```
2026-03-18T11:02:12Z kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13
2026-03-18T11:02:18Z kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13
```
not massive. but prometheus shows dozens in the same minute.
lucas-runtime: here's a quick grep from the collector logs: `for line in collector.log: if "Xid" in line: tags.append(line.split("|")[3])` — looks like a recent change added a trailing newline to the `device_id` tag, causing downstream grouping duplication.\jemily-devex: (typo: emily) I think collector PR #452 added tag normalization. Could be that rollback candidate.
ajay-sre: can we confirm which deploy time correlates? check release history.
maria-ops: deployment timeline: collector v2.9.4 rolled 03:58 UTC this morning. Alerts started ~04:10 UTC.
ops-oncall: reproducible locally: run collector against kernellog sample, you'll see duplicate metrics emitted with slightly different tag values (one with `\n` suffix). Prometheus treats them as distinct and sums them in the alerting rule.
lucas-runtime: so it's a telemetry parsing bug, not a fleet-wide hardware failure. Good catch. Immediate action: revert collector to v2.9.3 and backfill corrected metrics before unpausing drains.
ajay-sre: agreed. Maria — can you roll back? Also we should identify any nodes that were actually drained/replaced; we may need to requeue them.
maria-ops: starting rollback now: `infractl deploy rollback collector v2.9.3 --regions us-west2,us-central`
emily-devex: heads-up: rollback will reduce alert noise but there may still be genuine flaky cards mixed in. Need a cross-check: correlate with SMART/EC logs and ECC parity counters per PCI address before marking nodes healthy.
lucs-runtime: (lucas) writing a small script to compare kernel Xid counts vs prometheus series: `python compare_counts.py --source kernellogs --prom metrics --window 10m` — will run against samples and build a list.
ops-oncall: alerting followups: increase debounce on the ECC alert from 1m to 5m, and add a cross-source sanity check that requires both prometheus and kernel log spikes to pass for auto-drain to fire.
ajay-sre: good. Also add a secondary check that prevents mass simultaneous drains: cap drains to 10 nodes per 10m per region and queue the rest for manual review.
emily-devex: cost/impact note: capacity drop ~21% at peak; customer latency SLOs degraded for ~40 minutes while we paused. Need to calculate credits exposure. Finance pinged?\maria-ops: filing incident ticket INC-2026-042 to track customer impact and credit calc.
lucas-runtime: cleanup plan: 1) rollback collector (in progress), 2) re-evaluate metrics (10m), 3) identify legitimately drained nodes and requeue if safe, 4) tighten alert rules and drain rate-limits, 5) postmortem + root cause.\ops-oncall: rollback completed at 04:36 UTC. metric series look normalized now. prometheus shows counts back to baseline.
ajay-sre: start requeueing nodes that were evicted due to false-positive drains. Maria — list of drained node IDs?
maria-ops: pulled from audit: 117 nodes drained, 98 in us-west2, 19 in us-central. Creating a requeue job with staggered 1-min cadence to avoid sudden capacity burst: `for n in drained_nodes: k8s uncordon n; sleep 60`
emily-devex: be careful: some nodes were flagged by hardware team previously. Cross-check node metadata tags `hw_mark=bad`. Only requeue nodes without `hw_mark=bad`.
lucas-runtime: running the cross-correlation now; current output: 89 nodes look safe to requeue immediately, 28 require manual hardware inspection.
ajay-sre: proceed with staged requeue for 89 nodes. Hold the 28 for diagnostics.
ops-oncall: starting requeue pass. I'll throttle to 5 nodes/min to keep scheduler stable.
maria-ops: requeueing started at 05:02 UTC. First 15 nodes OK. Monitoring latency and queuing.
emily-devex: add follow-up actions: 1) revert PR #452 with note about trailing newline handling, 2) add unit test that strips whitespace on tags, 3) backfill aggregated metrics for billing/audit to avoid overstating error counts historically, 4) review auto-drain policy and add manual approval for >20 node drains.
ajay-sre: assign owners: lucas-runtime for backfill script, emily-devex for collector PR revert and tests, maria-ops for requeue and customer comms, ajay-sre for alert rule changes.
lucas-runtime: will also add grep-based kernel verification into the alert playbook: `journalctl -k | grep Xid | wc -l` tie threshold to prometheus before drain.
ops-oncall: requeue finished at 05:41 UTC. Net capacity restored to ~98% of baseline. No further Xid surge observed after rollback.
emily-devex: drafting postmortem. Initial summary: telemetry tag normalization bug introduced trailing newline that caused exaggerated metrics -> mass auto-drains -> capacity drop -> customer impact. Remediation: rollback, metric backfill, guard rails for auto-drain, unit tests and improved alert cross-check.
ajay-sre: good. Add SLA impact numbers and timeline. Also propose a simulated inject test in staging for telemetry changes to avoid regressions.
maria-ops: will open postmortem doc and link to INC-2026-042. Will also notify support/customer-success with suggested customer messaging.
lucas-runtime: additional note: we should add a histogram of per-device unique series count to detect tag explosion earlier.
emily-devex: thanks team. any outstanding blockers?
ajay-sre: none from infra side. closing thread once postmortem doc is linked.
monitoring-bot: NOTE: incident ticket INC-2026-042 created and linked to this thread.
